segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were out of Earlmere on three horses before the mist had come off the millpond. Elin Hargrove's father had handed over his plough mare without asking one question, which frightened her more than the hurry did. Dessa Fenwick rode in front and set the pace, and at the fork above the east cut she took them off the cart road entirely, up a drovers' track through the stumps.

segments.speaker: Garret Marsh
segments.text: That's not the Tollgate road.

segments.speaker: Dessa Fenwick
segments.text: No. The carters keep to the low way because a loaded cart cannot take this shoulder. We can. It comes out at the ford a good half day short of them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The track climbed hard for an hour. Elin kept one hand on the waxed pouch at her hip, where a single leaf off Jasper Lund's rack lay flat between two squares of card.

segments.speaker: Elin Hargrove
segments.text: Say we catch them. What then?

segments.speaker: Garret Marsh
segments.text: Then I tell the buyer what he's bought.

segments.speaker: Elin Hargrove
segments.text: You scrape a leaf with your thumbnail and smell it. I watched you do it and I still had to take your word. A Tollgate buyer with forty cords paid for will take the word of the man holding the money.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Garret said nothing for a while. The mare picked her way over loose stone.

segments.speaker: Garret Marsh
segments.text: And they'll say the old cutter from Earlmere is talking down another man's crop to raise the price of his own. It has been said before.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At the stream below the ridge they got down to water the horses. Elin crouched on the bank with her sleeves pushed back, and then she stopped with her hands in the cold.

segments.speaker: Elin Hargrove
segments.text: Last winter you had me sorting in the shed with no brazier. My fingers went dead and I breathed on them, and I breathed on the leaves as well, to see the veins through the frost.

segments.speaker: Garret Marsh
segments.text: I remember you complaining of it.

segments.speaker: Elin Hargrove
segments.text: The good ones went warm. Only a little, like a stone that's been in a pocket. The rejects stayed cold as a window latch and the fog sat on them. I never said it to anybody. I thought everyone knew.

segments.speaker: Garret Marsh
segments.text: Nobody knows it. Nobody has ever put it to the test.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He took a leaf from his own cord and gave it to her. Elin held it to her mouth and breathed. The mist across the glass thinned and was gone before she had counted three, and the vein ran silver under it, and the leaf was warm against her lip. She put it down and took Jasper's leaf out of the pouch.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fog sat on it. She counted to ten and it was still there, and the leaf stayed as cold as the stream water.

segments.speaker: Elin Hargrove
segments.text: Cold. It's still cold.

segments.speaker: Dessa Fenwick
segments.text: Do it again and let me see it this time.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She did it again. Dessa watched, and then put her hat back on and went for the horses without a word.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came down to the ford below Tollgate in the middle of the afternoon. The cart stood in the shallows with its wheels wet, and a man in a buyer's grey coat was counting bundles off the tail of it into a crate, two at a time, while the driver held the tally board. Garret put his heels in.

segments.speaker: Elin Hargrove
segments.text: Don't stop him with your word.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: said Elin, riding up level with him.

segments.speaker: Elin Hargrove
segments.text: Stop him with mine. Let me breathe on one in front of the lot of them.
